problem_motivation.content: The need for design, prediction, and control of advanced materials capable of withstanding severe irradiation and mechanical extremes.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: design, prediction and control of advanced materials beyond current material designs become paramount

problem_motivation.content: Materials capable of withstanding extreme radiation, temperature, and stress for economically viable fusion power plants remain a challenge, as current options like tungsten are compromised by helium bubble formation and neutron damage.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: One remaining challenge is that of materials, which can withstand extreme conditions of radiation, temperature, and stress, with long-term steady properties for the power plant to be economically viable

prior_approach.content: Previous studies recommend specific ranges for thermophysical parameters (enthalpy of mixing, atomic size difference, omega parameter) to form single-phase HEAs.
prior_approach.evidence_span: For that, the value for Δ H mix was recommended to be in the range of −15 to 5 kJ per mole, while δ should be smaller than 6.6 and Ω larger than 1.1 [26] , [27] .

prior_limitation.content: While reducing grain size helps, it suffers from thermal instability in pure materials, specifically the coarsening of nanocrystalline grains at application temperatures.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, this approach can suffer from some drawbacks in pure materials such as the thermal instability of the nanocrystalline grains (coarsening at the application temperature)

prior_limitation.content: A previously developed quaternary W-based RHEA (W-Ta-Cr-V) exhibited detrimental Cr- and V-rich precipitates that could cause embrittlement.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: However, this quaternary RHEA demonstrated Cr- and V-rich precipitates which could be detrimental to mechanical properties in terms of embrittlement.

rejected_alternative.content: The authors rejected adding Fe to the W-Ta-Cr-V HEA because it promoted undesired intermetallic phases and lowered the melting point.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: However, the addition of Fe in both low and high elemental concentrations promotes the formation of several undesired intermetallic phases instead of single-phase solid-solution, as well as lowering the melting point of the system. Due to failure of this approach, a quinary HEA was planned

inspiration_source.content: The design strategy was inspired by the VEC model showing BCC RHEAs are stable when VEC is below 4.4.
inspiration_source.evidence_span: Due to failure of this approach, a quinary HEA was planned considering the principles introduced by the VEC model. It has been shown that BCC RHEAs can exhibit high-stability and suitable mechanical properties when the VEC value remains below 4.4 [24] , [25] .

causal_claim.content: Grain refinement in the dual-beam case was caused by a cascade effect.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This suggests that such a grain refinement observed in the dual-beam irradiation case was caused by a cascade effect.

causal_claim.content: The increase in hardness after annealing is directly attributed to Hf segregation to grain boundaries.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The increase in hardness after annealing was ~3 GPa and this can be directly attributed to Hf segregation to grain boundaries as revealed in Fig. 2 and in the STEM-EDX mapping as insets in Fig. 5 .

mechanism_principle.content: The observed material response, including microstructural stability and improved irradiation resistance, is attributed to a combination of stable grain boundaries, chemical complexity altering defect recombination, and a decreased order-disorder transition temperature.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This material response can be attributed to a combination of factors, including the high density of stable grain boundaries (even showing grain refinement), chemical complexity altering defect recombination rates, and a decrease in the order-disorder transition temperature (ODTT) as compared to the original four elements RHEA.

mechanism_principle.content: Hardness increase after annealing is attributed to Hf segregation along grain boundaries.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Increase in hardness after annealing is solely associated with Hf segregation along the GBs

mechanism_principle.content: Hardness increase after irradiation is attributed to a synergistic combination of Ar implantation, lattice distortion, and grain refinement.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: whereas the increase after irradiation is a synergistic combination between Ar implantation, lattice distortion caused by irradiation ballistic mixing, and grain refinement.

mechanism_principle.content: High-energy recoil events divide into sub-cascades with diameters near the initial grain size, allowing fragmentation to occur.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Molecular dynamics simulations have shown that high-energy (50 keV) recoil events begin to divide in sub-cascades [34] , [35] , each with a diameter on the order of 10 nm. This upper limit on cascade size is near the initial grain-size of the W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf RHEA, allowing fragmentation to take place whereas, in coarser-grained materials, a similar event would likely result in defect migration to boundaries.

mechanism_principle.content: The rough energy landscape of He migration leads to quick site finding, binding, and clustering, resulting in smaller bubble nucleation and uniform distribution.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This rough energy landscape implies that He has a higher tendency to quickly find a fairly stable site that can act as a bubble nuclei, and also to bind to other slowly migrating He interstitial atoms. The clustering of He will slow them further down and a trend for smaller and lesser bubble nucleation will follow, and therefore, uniform bubble distribution with no preferential bubble formation at the grain boundaries or a wide distribution of bubble sizes occur.

mechanism_principle.content: Lattice distortion, enhanced by material homogenization from ordered to disordered state, can increase hardness.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: First, some change in hardness could be a result of material homogenization which occurred due to the transition from ordered to disordered state, as discussed above, and which enhances lattice distortion [52] .

mechanism_principle.content: Refinement of grain size in a very small initial grain size regime can result in a large change in hardness via the Hall-Petch transition.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Another factor that can cause a change in hardness in this HEA is the refinement of grain size when irradiated with heavy ion as demonstrated and illustrated earlier. As the grain size in this RHEA is very small (Fig. 3 ) and hardness follows a power law with grain size, a small refinement of grain size could result in a large change in hardness.

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors propose that a combined experimental and simulation methodology can successfully design a nanocrystalline RHEA system.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: through a combined experimental and simulation methodology, we design a nanocrystalline refractory high entropy alloy (RHEA) system

hypothesis_statement.content: The study proposes that a design strategy combining thermophysical parameter calculations, CALPHAD, and Cluster Expansion to add Hafnium to the W-Ta-Cr-V system will result in a quinary RHEA with higher irradiation resistance, high thermal stability, and no precipitation.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: In this study, a design strategy to further improve the overall response of the W-Ta-Cr-V RHEA is introduced and resulted in the development of a quinary RHEA with improved resistance to high-temperature and irradiation environments. The aim of such design is to develop a RHEA with higher irradiation resistance, high thermal stability, enhanced control over the morphology, and no precipitation at reactor-relevant temperatures.

hypothesis_statement.content: It is expected that the material will maintain structural integrity regarding grain size in a nuclear environment due to cascade-induced refinement.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Therefore, if used in a nuclear environment where cascades are expected due to highly energetic neutrons, this material is expected to keep its structural integrity in terms of grain size.

hypothesis_statement.content: Homogenized chemical distribution is expected after irradiation due to the relationship between ballistic mixing, SRO, and the ODTT.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Considering the irradiation-induced ballistic mixing and the corresponding atomic displacement and ordering [37] , homogenization can occur at lower temperatures. Therefore, we expect to see homogenized chemical distribution of the material after irradiation which was the case in this work.

hypothesis_statement.content: No precipitation is expected during irradiation for a specific composition at the given temperature because its ODTT is slightly lower.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: for that composition (W 29.4 Ta 42 Cr 5.0 V 16.1 Hf 7.5 ), the SRO and the corresponding atomic configurations (Figs. 6 and 7 ) showed a slightly smaller (1080 K) ODTT (but rather different behavior at lower temperatures) and, therefore, no precipitation is expected during irradiation at 1173 K.

hypothesis_statement.content: Different compositions with different SRO parameters and segregation behaviors are expected to have different mechanical properties.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: It also should be noted that different compositions of this alloy system can have different SRO parameters and different elemental segregation behavior (Figs. 6 and 7 ), and therefore, are expected to have different mechanical properties.

evidence_result.content: Experimental and in situ microscopy observations confirm high thermal stability and radiation resistance.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Compositions assessed under extreme environments and in situ electron-microscopy reveal both high thermal stability and radiation resistance

evidence_result.content: Specific observations of grain refinement under heavy ion irradiation, resistance to dual-beam irradiation and helium implantation, low defect generation/evolution, and no detectable grain growth.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We observe grain refinement under heavy ion irradiation and resistance to dual-beam irradiation and helium implantation in the form of low defect generation and evolution, as well as no detectable grain growth

evidence_result.content: The experimental and modeling results show good agreement.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The experimental and modeling results—showing a good agreement

evidence_result.content: Dual-beam irradiation caused grain refinement, reducing average grain size from 36.3 nm to 21.1 nm.
evidence_result.evidence_span: However, during the dual-beam irradiation, grain refinement occurred, and the average grain size dropped to 21.1 ± 1.4 nm after a total irradiation time of ~94 mins.

evidence_result.content: No dislocation loops were detected after 8.5 dpa and 9.13% He implantation during dual-beam irradiation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Dislocation loops were not detected even after 8.5 dpa and at 9.13% He implantation during the dual-beam experiment (Supplementary Movie 1 is attached to the supplementary material).

evidence_result.content: Sample hardness increased from 13.25 GPa (unirradiated) to 20 GPa after irradiation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: After annealing the sample hardness increased to 16.25 GPa, while after irradiation the sample hardness reached a value of 20 GPa.

evidence_result.content: The strongest atomic attraction is observed for the Cr-Hf pair, indicated by the most negative SRO parameter at low temperatures.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Among the considered pairs of atoms, the strongest attraction is observed for the Cr-Hf pair, which presents the most negative SRO parameter at low temperatures for both RHEAs.

evidence_result.content: The irradiated part of the APT needle showed homogenization of elements with no precipitation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The irradiated part showed homogenization of the elements and no precipitation.

evidence_result.content: No spherical precipitates were observed in TEM images and EDX for the in situ irradiated samples.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For the in situ irradiated samples, TEM images, and EDX showed no spherical precipitates

evidence_result.content: The hardness of the as-deposited sample was measured at 13.25 GPa.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The as-deposited sample had a hardness of 13.25 GPa.

evidence_result.content: The hardness increased by 3 GPa after annealing.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The increase in hardness after annealing was ~3 GPa

evidence_result.content: Hardness increased by a further 3.75 GPa after irradiation.
evidence_result.evidence_span: After irradiation, the hardness further increased by 3.75 GPa.

evidence_result.content: No dislocation loop formation was observed in the RHEA even under dual-beam conditions.
evidence_result.evidence_span: This RHEA possesses high irradiation resistance and shows no dislocation loop formation, even under dual-beam conditions

constraint.content: Hf concentration was kept minimal to avoid high activation under in-reactor conditions.
constraint.evidence_span: Due to its high melting point, Hf was firstly selected with a minimal concentration to avoid a material with high activation under in-reactor conditions

constraint.content: Displacement threshold energy fixed at 40 eV for all elements in SRIM simulations.
constraint.evidence_span: 40 eV [59] was taken as the displacement threshold energy for all elements.

constraint.content: Strain tensor magnitude limited to prevent large distortions during DFT relaxation.
constraint.evidence_span: checkrelax function was used to ensure the square-root sum of each element of the strain tensor squared no larger than 0.1.

constraint.content: Indentation depth constrained to avoid size effects given the irradiated layer thickness.
constraint.evidence_span: the hardness and modulus measurements were obtained at 200 nm indentation depth.

contradiction.content: The observed lack of precipitation contradicts the prediction of density and size of Cr-V precipitation based on SRO for the quaternary W-Ta-Cr-V RHEA, although the current work notes the quaternary alloy did predict precipitation.
contradiction.evidence_span: It should be stated that the SRO and atomic configurations of the W-Ta-Cr-V RHEA predicted both density and size of the Cr-V precipitation [22] .
